---
title: JanitorUtils
description: Janitor cleanup pattern utilities for automatic resource management.
---

Common cleanup helpers built on top of the Janitor library. Provides automatic cleanup when instances are removed from the game hierarchy.

## Usage

```luau
local ReplicatedStorage = game:GetService('ReplicatedStorage')
local JanitorUtils = require(ReplicatedStorage.Vendor.JanitorUtils)

-- Automatically clean up when object is destroyed
local bucket = JanitorUtils.TrackAncestry(myGui)

-- Add connections, instances, callbacks to bucket
bucket:Add(connection)
bucket:Add(part, 'Destroy')
```

## API Reference

### `JanitorUtils.TrackAncestry(obj: Instance): Janitor`

Creates a Janitor that automatically destroys itself when the given instance is removed from the game hierarchy.

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|-----------|------|-------------|
| `obj` | `Instance` | The instance to track for ancestry changes |

Returns a `Janitor` instance that will self-clean when `obj` is destroyed or parented to `nil`.

## Example

```luau
local ReplicatedStorage = game:GetService('ReplicatedStorage')
local JanitorUtils = require(ReplicatedStorage.Vendor.JanitorUtils)

local function setupUI(frame: Frame)
    local bucket = JanitorUtils.TrackAncestry(frame)

    -- Set up hover effects
    local hoverConn = frame.MouseEnter:Connect(function()
        frame.BackgroundColor3 = Color3.fromRGB(255, 255, 255)
    end)
    bucket:Add(hoverConn)

    -- Create temporary highlight
    local highlight = Instance.new('Highlight')
    highlight.Parent = frame
    bucket:Add(highlight, 'Destroy')

    -- No manual cleanup needed - bucket destroys itself when frame is removed
end
```

## When to Use

Use `TrackAncestry` when:
- Creating temporary UI components that need cleanup
- Setting up connections on instances that may be destroyed
- Managing resources tied to a specific instance's lifetime
- Building modular systems where cleanup should be automatic
